steps.title: Group the coast into three shapes
steps.text: Find the dark cliff, pale mist and distant horizon. Sketch those masses before adding detail.

steps.title: Separate near from far
steps.text: In grayscale, compare the darkest foreground with the softer distant forms. Keep that value gap in your study.

steps.title: Let edges describe the mist
steps.text: Restore color. Keep distant edges soft and reserve sharp accents for the foreground. Try a 60-second thumbnail.

steps.title: Read the mountain silhouettes
steps.text: Trace each outer contour with your eyes. Compare wide bases, narrow peaks and the empty spaces between them.

steps.title: Test the value groups
steps.text: Ignore small textures. Can the mountain layers still read as separate flat shapes in grayscale?

steps.title: Design one new silhouette
steps.text: Keep the same large-to-small rhythm, but invent a different peak. Compare its negative spaces with the reference.

steps.title: Find the light direction
steps.text: Follow the brightest planes around the harbor. Mark one light arrow before drawing individual buildings.

steps.title: Keep a clear focal contrast
steps.text: Use the grayscale view to locate the strongest light-dark boundary. Simplify weaker background contrasts.

steps.title: Compare warm and cool planes
steps.text: Return to color. Separate sunlit warm planes from cooler shadows, then paint a small three-color study.

lessons.title: Observation study: Tavern in Warm Backlight

steps.title: Read the tavern as silhouettes
steps.text: Find the large dark structures against the backlight. Draw their outline first, with no interior detail.

steps.title: Protect the bright opening
steps.text: In grayscale, compare the bright opening to the darkest framing shapes. Keep that relationship simple.

steps.title: Control the glowing edges
steps.text: Return to color. Soften edges near the warm light; keep only a few dark foreground edges crisp.

provenance.description: Silent Trace demo micro-lesson: original reference shown in full with authored observation exercises and a temporary grayscale inspection. Not an original-artist tutorial or a real instructor recording.

steps.title: Follow the action diagonals
steps.text: Look for the main slanted shapes carrying movement through the tavern. Reduce them to three directional marks.

steps.title: Check the focal value pattern
steps.text: In grayscale, find where the strongest contrast pulls your eye. Make quieter areas simpler in your thumbnail.

steps.title: Vary busy and quiet areas
steps.text: Restore color. Compare dense detail with open areas. Leave one calm region so the action remains readable.

steps.title: Block the cliff and outpost
steps.text: Compare the building mass with the cliff underneath it. Place their largest shapes before drawing windows.

steps.title: Separate the distance layers
steps.text: Inspect the grayscale view. Compare foreground, middle ground and sky as three value families.

steps.title: Choose a limited color key
steps.text: Return to color. Pick one dominant cool family and one warm accent, then paint the scene in five shapes.

steps.title: Organize the city by scale
steps.text: Find foreground, middle ground and distant skyline. Compare the size changes rather than counting buildings.

steps.title: Build a readable value map
steps.text: Squint at the grayscale city. Group neighboring buildings into large light and dark masses.

steps.title: Use depth before detail
steps.text: Restore color. Compare distant saturation and edge sharpness with the foreground. Apply that change to a thumbnail.

lessons.title: Observation study: Station in Warm Light

steps.title: Track the station perspective
steps.text: Follow the long architectural lines toward their meeting area. Establish that structure before adding signs.

steps.title: Locate the brightest route
steps.text: In grayscale, find how the light leads through the station. Preserve that path in a three-value sketch.

steps.title: Balance warm light and shadow
steps.text: Return to color. Compare sunlit surfaces with shaded planes. Save your strongest warmth for the focal area.

steps.title: Find the big winter shapes
steps.text: Separate the skyline, snow and street into large silhouettes. Notice how their shapes overlap.

steps.title: Measure atmospheric contrast
steps.text: In grayscale, compare the nearest darks with the softer distance. Reduce contrast as shapes recede.

steps.title: Keep snow color varied
steps.text: Return to color. Compare cool shadow snow with warmer light. Avoid using one white for every surface.

steps.title: Place the town inside its landscape
steps.text: Compare the town scale with mountains and water. Block those large relationships before roof details.

steps.title: Group the winter values
steps.text: In grayscale, separate the darkest structures from pale snow and atmosphere. Keep the distant layers simple.

steps.title: Study warm accents in cold light
steps.text: Return to color. Find small warm accents against the cool landscape. Use them sparingly in a quick study.

steps.title: Read the pose and silhouette
steps.text: Follow the head tilt, shoulder line and outer shape. Sketch the gesture before facial features or costume detail.

steps.title: Check the face and hair masses
steps.text: In grayscale, compare the large face, hair and clothing shapes. Keep their proportions readable without small lines.

steps.title: Choose expression-bearing edges
steps.text: Restore color. Compare the angles of brows, eyes and mouth. Change one angle in your own study and compare the mood.

steps.title: Start with the head gesture
steps.text: Notice the head tilt and the relationship of shoulders to face. Draw a simple action line before adding features.

steps.title: Compare large facial proportions
steps.text: In grayscale, compare the face outline, hair mass and spacing of features. Use light construction shapes first.

steps.title: Test one expression change
steps.text: Return to color. Compare brow and mouth angles. Try a small variation, then ask which marks changed the expression most.

steps.title: Follow the sky movement
steps.text: Trace the broad arcs through the sky. Plan their direction before painting individual dabs or stars.

steps.title: Separate light from dark masses
steps.text: In grayscale, compare bright sky paths with the dark cypress and village. Preserve these large value groups.

steps.title: Make dabs follow the form
steps.text: Restore color. Use short directional strokes in blue and yellow families. Compare where the direction changes.

lessons.title: Observation study: Wheat Field with Cypresses

steps.title: Compare field, tree and sky rhythms
steps.text: Follow the horizontal field, rising cypress and curling clouds. Give each area a distinct stroke direction.

steps.title: Check the tree silhouette
steps.text: In grayscale, compare the dark tree against its surroundings. Keep that silhouette clear before adding texture.

steps.title: Vary the short color dabs
steps.text: Return to color. Compare yellow-green field marks with cooler sky marks. Use varied dabs instead of a single flat fill.

lessons.title: Observation study: Café Terrace at Night

steps.title: Find the cafe perspective
steps.text: Follow the terrace edges into the street. Sketch the large perspective wedge before tables or cobblestones.

steps.title: Protect the bright cafe shape
steps.text: In grayscale, compare the lit canopy with the dark street. Keep the main value contrast stronger than small details.

steps.title: Compare yellow with blue
steps.text: Restore color. Observe warm cafe light against cool night colors. Try the same contrast with a limited palette.

steps.title: Group the floating color patches
steps.text: Separate large water reflections from smaller lily shapes. Place their spacing before painting individual petals.

steps.title: Look for quiet value changes
steps.text: In grayscale, compare the subtle dark and light patches. Avoid outlining every lily with the same hard edge.

steps.title: Let adjacent colors build the water
steps.text: Return to color. Compare blue, green and violet patches. Paint beside earlier marks and keep some edges soft.

steps.title: Simplify boats and horizon
steps.text: Place the horizon and boat silhouettes as a few broad shapes. Keep the distant industrial detail secondary.

steps.title: Compare the sun in grayscale
steps.text: Notice how the sun value compares with the haze. Ask how much its color, rather than outline, attracts your eye.

steps.title: Use one small warm accent
steps.text: Restore color. Compare orange against muted blue-gray water. Keep broken reflection marks small and horizontal.

lessons.title: Observation study: The Artist’s Garden at Giverny

steps.title: Find the garden depth rhythm
steps.text: Follow the planted rows into the distance. Compare the broad foreground color patches with smaller distant marks.

steps.title: Group the shaded passages
steps.text: In grayscale, locate the darker trees and path. Let these large groups organize the busy flower texture.

steps.title: Suggest flowers with color patches
steps.text: Return to color. Place neighboring greens, violets and warm accents. Soften distant edges instead of drawing every flower.
